items.item: Stage columns run in hiring order (such as Applied → Screening → Interview → Offer → Hired), and rejected or withdrawn candidates are kept out of the active columns, in a separate collapsed column or behind a filter
items.evidence: STAGES = [applied, screening, interview, offer, hired] rendered in order via columnTemplate; DECLINED_STAGE ('Not moving forward') is only appended to columns when state.showDeclined is true, toggled by #toggleDeclined ('Show not moving forward'), default false so declined/withdrawn candidates are hidden behind this filter.

items.item: Each stage header shows a candidate count that matches the number of cards in that column under the current filters
items.evidence: renderBoard() computes `cards = filtered.filter(c => c.stage === stage.key)` from the same `filtered` list used to render cards, and columnTemplate prints `cards.length` in the header badge, e.g. '' + cards.length + ''.

items.item: The page names the opening being shown (job title, department, positions to fill and hired so far, such as "Senior Accountant · Finance · 1 of 2 hired"), and a selector switches to another opening
items.evidence: renderJobMeta() shows job.title, department + ' team', location, type, manager, 'N openings', and 'Opened N days ago' — e.g. screenshot shows 'Design team | Remote (US) | Full-time | Hiring manager Dana Whitfield | 2 openings | Opened 48 days ago'. There is no 'X of Y hired' figure anywhere, only total openings. #jobSwitcher select does switch openings correctly, but the hired-so-far count required by the item is missing.

items.item: Each card gives the candidate's name, application source and days in the current stage, and candidates who have stayed past a stated limit are flagged with a text label or icon rather than colour alone
items.evidence: cardTemplate renders name, 'From ' + c.source + '.' and days + ' day(s) in ' + stageLabel. However the only badges are flag==='new' ('New') and flag==='offer-out' ('Offer sent') — there is no concept of a stated time-in-stage limit anywhere in the code, so overdue candidates are never flagged by label or icon.

items.item: A card can change stage without dragging, through a "Move to" menu or buttons that work from the keyboard, and each move is announced through an aria-live region
items.evidence: renderDossierActions() renders a button 'Move to ' + next.label that calls moveCandidate(); cards are reachable/openable via keyboard (tabindex="0", role="button", Enter/Space handled in board keydown listener) and dossier buttons are native <button> elements. showToast() writes into `#toast` which has `aria-live="polite"`, and moveCandidate() calls showToast('Moved ' + c.name + ' to ' + ... + '.') on every move.

items.item: Moving a candidate to Rejected opens a confirmation that names the candidate and requires a rejection reason before it completes
items.evidence: The decline action is `else if (action === 'decline') { moveCandidate(c, 'declined'); }` — it moves the candidate immediately with no confirmation dialog and no input for a rejection reason; declinedReason only exists as pre-seeded static data in CANDIDATES_RAW, never captured via UI.

items.item: Search by candidate name or email and filters by source and by recruiter narrow the board, and the active filters are displayed with a way to clear them
items.evidence: matchesFilters() builds `hay` from name + title + company + tags only (no email field), and #searchInput's placeholder is 'Search by name, title, or skill'. #filterSource and #filterRecruiter do narrow the board. But there is no active-filter display or clear control anywhere — only #activeCount showing a result count, with no chips/labels for which filters are applied and no 'clear filters' affordance.

items.item: Opening a card shows the candidate's contact details, a link to the CV and a stage history listing each move with its date and the person who made it
items.evidence: renderDossierContent() shows email/phone/linkedin as plain text (not <a> links), and the resume is shown as `<span>` text c.resumeFile with 'Preview not available in this demo.' (not a link). stageTimelineHtml() lists stage + fmtDate(date) only — history entries are {stage, date} with no person/recruiter attached, so no mover is shown.

items.item: A stage with no candidates keeps its column and shows a placeholder such as "No candidates", and loading and error-with-retry states are built in
items.evidence:
columnTemplate always renders a column per stage and shows '

No candidates match your filters.

' when cards.length is 0, satisfying the placeholder half. But the app uses only static in-memory CANDIDATES_RAW with no fetch/async logic, so there is no loading state and no error-with-retry state anywhere in the code.

notes: Board data is fully static/in-memory (no fetch), so there is no real loading or error state to evaluate — only the empty-column placeholder is implemented. The UI is largely custom-styled (serif/sans pairing, muted stage colors, small radii) and didn't show obvious generic-dashboard template tells from the checklist list.
